conclusion: PHYSICAL / CAMERA CAPTURE. E12 analysed 7 finalized session(s); 4 delivered the complete SHA-verified payload. Baseline repeats: 3 session(s), repeatable=True (throughput CV 0.0). For the reference transfer the gross channel rate is 1199.88 bps, gross payload 879.91 bps, RS(255,223) goodput 769.49 bps and application throughput 99.44 bps. The application carries 1.243 bytes per displayed frame out of 11 (11.30%). The RS-to-application gap is 670.05 bps: framing 319.97 bps, RS parity 110.42 bps, unused packet capacity 677.27 bps, with compression recovering 7.21 bps. The dominant loss is application payload utilisation (unused packet capacity) at 677.27 bps (56.4% of the gross channel). Camera capture and decode have measured headroom; RS corrections and packet loss are zero; detection/CRC failures did not reduce unique-frame delivery. Across the three independent baselines, unique-frame delivery ranged 0.965-1.000 and camera-sample CRC rate ranged 0.618-0.889, yet all three recovered the exact payload; the one baseline that lost 9 frames was repaired by 18 RS symbols. The panel ran at 9.999 fps, not 60 Hz; the 6x difference is a playback choice, and 60 fps values are projections, not measurements. Brightness was set and read back at [0.65, 0.9] fractions, but both brightness sessions lost the fiducials to hand-held framing drift after about 14 s ([455, 457] detection failures; unique-frame delivery [0.686, 0.573]), so no brightness effect is claimed; that is a measured receiver reliability failure, not a brightness result. Distance, angle and ambient illuminance remain UNMEASURED. All measured numbers come from preserved camera files; projections are labelled separately.

definitions.rs_goodput_bps: 2,453 RS data bytes/packet x 8 / (255 frames / observed display fps)
